Title: Donald Trump's wild week as he bans media from White House and brags over Greenland 'deal'
Article_Text:
Donald Trump's wild week as he bans media from White House and brags over Greenland 'deal'
Donald Trump has suffered a series of humiliations over the last few weeks. From the Supreme Court ruling his plan to screw up the midterms by making postal voting insanely complicated couldn't be implemented in time, to his hand-picked Fed chair voting through a rate increase...to another judge saying he can't write his name on the memorial to a dead president, it's been defeat after defeat.
And despite offering the American people a $5,000 bribe each and urging them to pretend he's on the ballot, it looks increasingly like his Republican Party is going to lose both houses of Congress in November's election.
And when you're an old man backed into a corner, being told left and right that you can't do the things you want to do, you grab onto pretty much anything you can control.
And that's probably why Trump announced last night that three news outlets would be banned from the White House and made out a fairly benign treaty extension with Denmark was a major shift in power over Greenland.
Here's how Trump's week spiralled, and how he's now trying to claw his way back.
"Oh, the ban on the free press?"
Donald Trump last night announced he was throwing CNN, Politico and MS Now out of the White House, something he genuinely referred to as a "ban on the free press."
Why? Well, because he doesn't like the things they write.
Claiming the outlets were "unfair" and "dishonest", Trump said it was a "very simple ban. I don't want them in my office, I don't want them here. I would say the ban will go as far as you can. If they could straighten themselves out I'd love it."
He went on to warn the New York Times and Washington Post they could be next.
Trump tried to ban now former CNN reporter Jim Acosta from the White House during his first term, taking his White House pass away from him.
But the move was blocked by a federal court after Acosta argued it infringed on his rights under the first amendment (freedom of the press) and fifth amendment (due process).
Asked if he was trying to "intimidate" the press, Trump said: "No, no, no. I dislike dishonest press, like you, I think you're terrible. I like to see honest press."
Asked how the move was constitutional, Trump said: "I don't think someone should be allowed to come in and write fake stories....It's sick. There's something wrong with a country that can allow people to write purposely negative stories. Now, if they want to write them that's fine, but I don't have to let them into my...into the people's house."
At the time of writing, reporters are starting to arrive at the White House to find their passes have been deactivated.
As it stands, CNN is still down to be the nominated pool outlet travelling with Trump on Monday, so we'll see.
"We've got Greenland!"
Trump last night posted a message on Truth Social that seemed to suggest Denmark had kind of given Greenland to the US. He followed that up by posting a map of the country overlaid with the Stars and Stripes.
And it's certainly been taken that way by a decent chunk of MAGA - with Utah Senator Mike Lee tweeting: "We've got Greenland! This is what winning looks like."
But it ain't really so, though, Joe.
Trump said on Friday that the agreement would give the United States “permanent control over security, and all other needs, in Greenland, completely addressing ALL of our many US concerns.”Denmark and the US already have a long-standing security agreement that has allowed the US to deploy forces in Greenland, and it was not immediately clear how this deal was different from that.
The deal is expected to be signed at the UN General Assembly in New York, which Trump will attend from Monday.
"Sometimes a wedding gift is simply a wedding gift"
So you might remember earlier this year that Donald Trump's adult son, Don Jr, got married for the second time. It made a bit of news at the time, because the ceremony took place in the Bahamas and Trump...the father of the groom...did not go.
His excuse was that he was a little busy with the Iran war. And, sure, maybe.
But we learned this week that while the wedding itself was a smallish affair in a chapel on a private island, there was a two-day after party on a different island, which was paid for by Umar Kremlev a Russian Oligarch with close ties to Vladimir Putin.
The island rents for about a hundred thousand dollars a night, and other costs covered by Kremlev are said to have included a fireworks display that cost another 70 grand.
Jr's new wife Bettina, described Kremlev as a "dear friend" and said he "very generously hosted two incredible nights of celebrations for us after our wedding."
She went on to say: "It was an extraordinarily generous wedding gift from a friend, and something for which we were and remain incredibly grateful"
Jr's people said he and Kremlev are "personal friends" but don't have a business relationship.
And the happy couple added: "It's unfortunate that something so personal and happy can be recast as something political or sinister simply because of who someone is or where they come from.
"Friendship doesn't require a political motive. Generosity doesn't automatically come with an agenda. And sometimes a wedding gift is simply a wedding gift."
So who is this guy? Well, Kremlev runs the International Boxing Association, which is funded by the Russian state-backed energy firm Gazprom.
The group has been suspended by the Olympics, in part, for failing to report its ties to Gazprom.
As recently as this year, Kremlev was part of a Russian delegation to China led by Putin himself. Putin has also given Kremlev the Order of Friendship, one of the Russian Federation's highest honours.
Donald Trump senior said: "I have no idea who Umar is, never heard of him, and he didn't pay for Don and Bettina's wedding, which took place at a totally different location, and on a different day."
And last night in the Oval Office Trump said he had "heard" that Don Jr had reimbursed Kremlev for the cost of the festivities - which, assuming it's true (and we shouldn't assume that...) raises the question of...why? If it's all totally above board and fine, why pay it back?
Also, the Trump family is, famously, a billionaire family. Jr's personal net worth is in the region of $300 million.
Why didn't he just pay for his own party? I suspect we'll find out one day. Maybe some time before the LA Olympics.
"I think the Trump administration should be recognised as having saved the Kennedy Center"
Long term readers will recall that Donald Trump has an obsession with the Kennedy Centre.
For newcomers, a quick recap: The Kennedy Centre is - or was - America's most renowned performing arts venue and organisation. A bit like The Barbican, except it's also the official national monument for John F Kennedy - one of America's most beloved presidents. A President, we should note, whose disappointing adult nephew serves in Trump's cabinet. More of him in a moment.
Trump set his sights on it from day one of his second Presidency, mounting a coup to stuff the board with his own cronies and installing himself as chairman. He set about reforming it in his own image, changing the programme in a way that prompted a huge backlash plunging ticket sales. He also, in the dead of night, added his own name above the door - so it was officially called the Donald J Trump and the John F Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts. Literally people woke up to find he'd slapped his name on a presidential memorial. Why is he so obsessed with taking over this hallowed institution? Well, nobody really knows. But throughout history dictators have seized control of the creative arts to suppress dissent and break up alternatives to state propaganda. To be clear, I'm not saying Trump is a dictator. But I am saying he's read a few pages from the big book of things that dictators do.
Anyway, the courts, unsurprisingly told him, nah, can't do that. See congress if you want to change the name. So the name had to come down. Fast forward to a month or so ago and Trump's handpicked board came up with another plan. According to them, the building is in drastic need of repair. Now, we only have their word and some CCTV footage of bits falling off the ceiling for that. And this is the trump administration, so we definitely shouldn't take that at face value. Remember the thing with the reflecting pool?
They said Trump was willing to close the centre for repairs, and he'd ensure the funding was there to renovate - IF the courts agree to put his name back up on the wall. In smaller letters this time, and underneath JFK's name rather than on top. And a federal judge blocked both the closure and the name change.
On Tuesday, the board closed the building anyway, in defiance of the judge's ruling. The same day, there was a reportedly chaotic meeting of the centre's board, during which they voted for a third time to close the building. This was opposed by Representative Joyce Beatty, a Democrat ex officio board member, who is behind the lawsuit that is blocking the process in the courts.
After that, Trump issued a pretty ominous statement on Truth Social. If the courts ruled against his appeal, and refused to let him put his name on the wall, he said, "the reconstruction and the renovation of the Kennedy Center will not take place." The centre would close "immediately" - and there was no indication of when...or if.. it would reopen.
And then came the photos. Trump landed at Andrews Air Force Base after a speech in North Carolina, and a photographer snapped him looking at a big poster board, on which is clearly written "Kennedy Center DEMOLISHED". The picture isn't clear, but it appears to be a manipulated image of the centre.
Speaking from the Oval Office, Trump said he was willing to save the centre, which he claimed was losing money. He did not address a question about demolishing it.
“We have a lot of people working very hard on it to save it," he said. "I can save it easily, but why should we be doing that and then raise money for the rest of our lives to keep it afloat? Because that’s what you have to do, if we get no recognition. I think the Trump administration should be recognised as having saved the Kennedy Center.”
Later last night, supporters and patrons descended on the legendary building, forming a human chain around it in protest against Trump's apparent plans.
Remember what happened with the East Wing. Do not be surprised if you wake up one morning in the near future to see footage of bulldozers.
"You've got a friend in the White House"
Robert F Kennedy Jr told members of an anti-vaccine group he founded that they have a "steadfast friend at the White House".
RFK, who is Donald Trump's health secretary, was speaking at a convention of Children's Health Defense, which he led for nearly a decade.
His speech came after four people did of measles in Pennsylvania, in the worst outbreak of the disease in decades.
"Let me be clear: You have a strong and steadfast friend in the White House. We've accomplished in 19 months things that would have seemed unthinkable two years ago," he said.
Kennedy, who is not a medical professional, raised a string of baseless questions about long-established vaccine safety.
He boasted about how the Trump administration, under his guidance, had limited the number of life-saving vaccines routinely given to children in the US - including scrapping regular shots for hepatitis A and B and meningococcal, the rare virus that causes meningitis.
President Trump has made repeated and unfounded claims that the vaccine scheme was "dangerous" and contributed to increased autism diagnoses.
And Trump suggested falsely that the Measles, Mumps and Rubella (MMR) vaccine could be "quite lethal" if taken as combined injection, and called for it to be split in to three separate shots.
Some 3,294 cases of measles have been confirmed in the US so far in 2026, up from 2,289 in the whole of 2025. according to the Centers for Disease Control (CDC). Nearly half of the 2026 cases (45%) were in children and young people aged 5-19, with 18% of the cases affecting the under 5s.
Some 95% of the cases were in unvaccinated people, or people whose vaccination status was unknown. Just 3% had had both doses of MMR. Of the 2026 cases, 267 people were hospitalised, including 66 children under 5.
In 2024, the year before Trump returned to office, there were 285 cases, and in 2023 just 59. More cases of measles have been confirmed in the US so far this year than in the decade from 2014 to 2024.
RFK spoke alongside Andrew Wakefield, the disgraced British former doctor whose fabricated research first popularised the false claim that the MMR vaccine is linked to autism.
After being struck off in the UK, and ostracised by the medical community, Wakefield moved to the US, where he has since become a minor celebrity in the anti-vaccine world.

Title: Why Carl From Resident Evil Looks So Familiar
Article_Text:
Why Carl From Resident Evil Looks So Familiar
After wowing audiences with the incredible one-two punch of "Barbarian" and the Oscar-winning "Weapons," Zach Cregger decided to go with something a bit different for his latest film and deliver a video game adaptation. "Resident Evil" is not a direct adaptation of any of the games from the iconic horror franchise, but it understands the true appeal of the best games in the series, embracing its iconography while doing something new with it.
The film is set during the events of "Resident Evil 2" while moving the timeline to the modern era. It follows Austin Abrams' Bryan, a medical courier trapped in Raccoon City in the middle of a viral outbreak that turns people into bloodthirsty monsters. Though Abrams carries much of the story on his shoulders, the film does have a supporting cast of characters, including Carl, who works with the Umbrella corporation.
If you saw "Resident Evil" and kept wondering why Carl looked so familiar, that's because he's played by Golden Globe and Emmy winner Paul Walter Hauser, best known for his roles in "I, Tonya," "Cobra Kai," "Black Bird" and "Fantastic Four." Or, in the case of true sickos, Paul Walter Hauser is known for being quite the decent indie wrestler with a penchant for bloody and thrilling matches.
Paul Walter Hauser has been delighting audiences for 20 years
Paul Walter Hauser got his start back in 2005, voicing various roles in "Too Late with Adam Carolla." He worked steadily on TV, with roles in "Community," "Key & Peele," and "It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia." It wasn't until 2017 with "I, Tonya," however, that Hauser finally got mainstream recognition for his dramatic and comedic skills. Since then, the actor has had memorable supporting roles in movies from acclaimed auteurs, appearing in Spike Lee's "BlacKkKlansman," and starring in Clint Eastwood's "Richard Jewell." He had a hilarious role in "The Naked Gun," was in "The Fantastic Four: First Steps," and became an essential part of "Cobra Kai."
Hauser, in addition to being a great comedic actor and a very capable dramatic performer, is also an indie professional wrestler. His Emmy acceptance speech was essentially a wrestling promo, calling out two legends for a match. Though we've seen many wrestlers become actors, and plenty of celebrities doing a wrestling sting for publicity or just fun, Hauser is not just dedicated to the world of wrestling but is quite compelling in the ring. He won the PROGRESS Proteus Title in 2025 and wore the belt to the premiere of "Fantastic Four." His match against QT Marshall at Ring of Honor's "Death Before Dishonor" was violent and gnarly, worthy of a former Cobra Kai student. This is to say, Hauser needs to do more wrestling, because the guy is hugely entertaining to watch.
After "Resident Evil," Hauser is set to appear in Netflix's "Scooby-Doo: Origins" TV series as a previous owner of the titular Great Dane.

Title: Phillies turn to improving Andrew Painter in clash vs. Mets
Article_Text:
Field Level Media
                
19 Sep 2026, 17:35 GMT+10
            
(Photo credit: Dale Zanine)
Christian Scott, Zac Thornton and Nolan McLean are providing the New York Mets hope that they eventually will be part of a rotation for a playoff contender.
The Philadelphia Phillies need rookie Andrew Painter to continue proving that now.
Painter will take the mound for the Phillies on Saturday afternoon when they visit the Mets in the third contest of a four-game series between the National League East rivals.
Painter (3-9, 5.54 ERA) will oppose Scott (4-5, 3.76) in a battle of right-handers.
The Phillies missed a chance to take over sole possession of the top wild-card spot in the NL on Friday night, when Thornton and two relievers combined on a six-hitter in the Mets' 6-3 win.
The Phillies, Chicago Cubs and San Diego Padres are tied for the NL's three wild-card spots at 85-69. The Cubs lost to the Cincinnati Reds 6-4 before the Padres created the three-way tie hours later with an 8-2 win over the Miami Marlins.
The Arizona Diamondbacks reside five games behind the Phillies, Cubs and Padres.
The importance of Painter was further magnified Friday, when Philadelphia fell to 0-2 in bullpen games necessitated by the absence of left-hander Jesus Luzardo (shoulder, 15-day injured list).
The All-Star was scratched from his scheduled start against the Atlanta Braves last Saturday, when the Phillies used six pitchers as the Braves rolled to a 12-2 win. On Friday, opener Tim Mayza got just one out and allowed three runs while pitching in Luzardo's spot.
The Phillies' bullpen also is being taxed by injury and ineffectiveness.
Right-hander Jonathan Bowlan departed Thursday's game vs. the Mets with a tight right groin. On Friday, Orion Kerkering gave up Juan Soto's three-run blast in the sixth inning -- the second homer surrendered by Kerkering in his last three outings, during which he has a 13.50 ERA.
'Anybody that gives up runs, when things aren't going good, your confidence is not sky high like when you're getting all your outs and everything's going smoothly,' Phillies interim manager Don Mattingly said. 'But we've got to get past that at this point.'
Painter is 2-1 with a 3.58 ERA in nine starts since being recalled from Triple-A Lehigh Valley on July 31. He didn't factor into the decision in his most recent start last Sunday, when he gave up one run over five innings as the Phillies beat the Braves 9-4. He has yet to face the Mets in his career.
The Mets (70-84) have been under .500 since April and officially were eliminated from playoff contention earlier this week. But McLean and Thornton continued to provide optimism for 2027 by combining to allow just three runs over 12 innings in the first two games of the series.
McLean took the hard-luck loss Thursday, when he gave up one run in six innings in the Phillies' 3-0 win.
Thornton, McLean and Scott have a combined 3.40 ERA in 66 starts. Thornton and McLean are rookies while Scott is in his second big-league season after Tommy John surgery cut his 2024 campaign short.
'I think you have to train like you've never won anything and compete like you've never lost,' Mets interim manager Andy Green said Friday night about Thornton. 'I think you have to live in that space constantly.'
Scott took the defeat Sunday after allowing two runs over six innings in the Mets' 2-0 loss to the New York Yankees. He is 1-0 with a 1.80 ERA in two career starts against the Phillies.

Title: Ed Sheeran Readies His Return to Stage for 1st Time Since Macklemore Was Cut and Other Acts Withdrew
Article_Text:
PHILADELPHIA (AP) — Ed Sheeran is set to resume his tour Saturday — possibly solo — after all his supporting acts withdrew in solidarity with opener Macklemore, who was dropped after making pro-Palestinian comments onstage.
It remains to be seen how Sheeran will handle the performance at Philadelphia’s Lincoln Financial Field given the departure of his opening acts and supporting band. Sheeran has performed much of his Loop Tour concerts solo, but he had been joined for several songs at each stop by the Irish folk band Beoga. Macklemore, Sheeran’s original U.S. opener, had been replaced by Danish band Lukas Graham and Irish singer Aaron Rowe before they backed out.
Finneas, Billie Eilish’s brother and musical collaborator, was due to tour with Sheeran in South America later this year before he too dropped out earlier this week.
Sheeran has not said anything publicly since losing the artists’ support. As of Friday, tickets were still available for Saturday’s show, and his website did not list any replacement acts. A coalition of pro-Palestinian organizations plans to protest outside the show Saturday afternoon.
The show comes after a tumultuous week that opened with Macklemore being dropped in response to exclaiming “Free Palestine” during a Sept. 5 show in New Jersey. Sheeran has said he was not responsible for the decision, which came at the urging of New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft. His company owns a stadium where Sheeran’s tour was scheduled to play on Friday.
Within hours of Sheeran’s statement Tuesday, his supporting acts withdrew.
Macklemore said Wednesday he is donating $1 million to support Palestinian relief efforts and called on Kraft to match the gift; a spokesperson for Kraft has said the billionaire and Sheeran have each agreed to donate $2 million but have not specified where the money will be directed. Sheeran’s representatives have not responded to multiple requests for comment.
Sheeran’s Loop Tour was the highest-grossing in the world, with an average box office gross of over $7 million per city, Pollstar said in May. Through the end of 2025, Sheeran was the No. 3 top-earning concert act since 2021.
Sheeran has said the tour promoter was ultimately responsible for the decision to drop Macklemore.
The Grammy winner was adamant in his Tuesday statement that he wouldn’t be drawn into discussion of the war in Gaza, arguing that his fans don’t come to his shows to hear about these issues.
He also said he “spoke with the venues at length all week to try to build a bridge” before Macklemore was dropped. He insisted he would never willingly let down his fans or abandon the touring crew and others who rely on him to make a living.
While promoters and venues wield great power over concert tours, experts say an artist of Sheeran’s magnitude generally has the final say about what happens concerning the shows.

Title: Questions remain over ICE arrests involving workers at Geisinger project
Article_Text:
Questions remain over ICE arrests involving workers at Geisinger project
DANVILLE, MONTOUR CO. (WOLF) — More than two weeks after federal immigration enforcement activity involving workers from a major construction project at Geisinger Medical Center, questions remain about how many people were taken into custody and the role local police played in the operation.
The enforcement activity took place Sept. 2 near Geisinger's Danville campus, where an estimated $880 million expansion is underway.
Immigrant advocacy organizations have said more than 40 workers were detained after leaving the construction project that day. Additional arrests were reported in the Danville area several days later.
U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, however, has provided a substantially lower number.
ICE has said 10 people were arrested in Danville and has maintained that the arrests occurred away from the Geisinger campus. The agency also said those arrested did not have active Temporary Protected Status or valid immigration parole.
The Pennsylvania Capital-Star reported Friday that it remains unclear whether ICE's count includes everyone taken into custody during the enforcement activity.
A construction worker interviewed by the Capital-Star said a number of Latino workers did not return to the project following the Sept. 2 operation. The worker said he personally knew of roughly 10 people from his company who were missing from the job, while workers from other contractors also failed to return.
However, the number of people who stopped reporting to work does not establish how many were arrested. Some workers may have left the area or decided not to return to the project.
Local police departments also assisted federal immigration authorities.
Mahoning Township Police Chief Frederick Dyroff III told the Capital-Star that his officers were conducting traffic enforcement near the Geisinger campus and turned five people over to federal authorities.
Dyroff said officers were positioned roughly a quarter-mile to a half-mile from Geisinger property. Danville Police Chief Greg Watson told the news organization that his department was also aware of the federal operation and that local officers have worked with ICE.
Both the Mahoning Township and Danville police departments participate in ICE's 287(g) program, which allows designated local law enforcement officers to perform certain immigration-enforcement functions in cooperation with the federal agency.
Geisinger has maintained that the enforcement activity did not occur on its property.
The health system said the people involved appeared to be workers associated with construction of its new patient tower. Geisinger uses a construction manager for the project and said ensuring workers meet federal and state employment eligibility requirements is the responsibility of that contractor.
The hospital expansion includes an 11-story patient tower, a larger emergency department, new operating rooms and 192 patient rooms.
Another unresolved issue involves records documenting the enforcement operation.
The Capital-Star reported that efforts to obtain local police records connected with at least one traffic stop have produced little information. The Pennsylvania NewsMedia Association told the publication that agreements between ICE and local departments can complicate efforts to obtain records involving joint immigration enforcement.
Several Pennsylvania members of Congress have separately raised concerns about the availability of information involving ICE partnerships with local police departments.
For now, accounts from federal authorities, local police, workers and immigrant advocacy organizations have not produced a definitive public accounting of how many people were detained in connection with the Danville operation.

Title: Yanks move on without Aaron Judge as D-backs fight to stay alive
Article_Text:
Field Level Media
                
19 Sep 2026, 19:49 GMT+10
            
(Photo credit: Kirby Lee)
The New York Yankees will play the rest of the regular season without slugger Aaron Judge. While they understand the magnitude of his loss, they enter the stretch run with belief.
The Yanks scored five runs in the first inning of a 9-2 victory over the Arizona Diamondbacks in the first game of a weekend series Friday, and the teams meet again Saturday in Phoenix as Arizona attempts to stay alive in the National League wild-card race.
'Obviously losing 'Judgey' hurts,' Cody Bellinger said. 'We all know he's the best hitter in the game. For us in here, our mindset is we're going to have to find a way. The talent in this room speaks for itself.
'I'm fully confident we have enough talent in here that we can go out and win and beat anybody.'
American League Cy Young favorite Cam Schlittler (14-6, 1.95 ERA) will face Arizona right-hander Brandon Pfaadt (7-3, 3.77) in the second game of the series.
The Diamondbacks (80-74) will ask Pfaadt to end a slump in which they have lost five of six. They are five games behind San Diego, the Chicago Cubs and Philadelphia (all 85-69) for the three NL wild-card spots with eight games to play.
'We know where we're at,' Arizona manager Torey Lovullo said. 'We can't afford to worry about things we can't control. I'm going to say there's time. There's always time.'
The Yankees (89-64) are 48-39 this season without Judge, who was placed on the injured list Friday with a strained right calf after missing three months earlier with a fractured right rib.
New York is also without injured regulars Jazz Chisholm Jr. (thumb) and Trent Grisham (hamstring), although manager Aaron Boone said Chisholm could return for the Tampa Bay series early next week.
The Yankees, who already have qualified for the postseason, are four games behind Tampa Bay in the AL East, and the teams have a four-game series at Yankee Stadium beginning Tuesday.
'There is no replacing a player as great as Aaron Judge, but we have high expectations that don't change now,' Boone said. 'One thing we do know is that we are in the dance.
'We've been built on the strength of our starting pitching all year.'
No one has been as strong as Schlittler, who is in his first full season and has made every start while Max Fried, Gerrit Cole and Carlos Rodon have missed time with injuries or recovery time.
Schlittler has won four of his last five starts and has given up one run or fewer in each of his last seven. He was struck on the back of his right leg by Bo Bichette's 111.5 mph comebacker on his 94th and last pitch of a 2-0 victory over the New York Mets last Sunday, but shrugged it off.
'You have an ace at the top that has pitched like that,' Boone said. 'That's a good place to start. He's been dominant. This is largely in line with who we saw down the stretch last year.'
Schlittler has never faced the Diamondbacks, although Jesus Sanchez is 4 for 12 with three walks against him.
Pfaadt is 0-2 with a 5.74 ERA in his last five starts, and he gave up six runs and 10 hits in 6 2/3 innings in a loss to Texas on Aug. 12. He will be pitching on six days' rest after being pushed back so Eduardo Rodriguez could start the first game of the series.
Pfaadt lost his only outing against the Yankees, giving up six runs in 4 1/3 innings of a 7-1 loss as a rookie in 2023. Cody Bellinger is 2 for 7 with two solo homers against him and Luis Garcia Jr. is 3 for 7 with a homer.

Commanders vs. Cowboys Score Prediction for NFL Week 2 (Does Dallas Bounce Back at Home?)
In this story:
Both the Dallas Cowboys and Washington Commanders lost road division games in Week 1 of the 2026 season, and they’re looking to bounce back in an afternoon matchup in Dallas on Sunday.
The Cowboys and Dak Prescott are favored at home, where they went 4-3-1 in the 2025 campaign. Dallas’ defense is a major concern ahead of Week 2, as it had the worst unit in the NFL in 2025 and allowed the New York Giants to walk all over them in Week 1.
Dallas was 30th in EPA/Play and 31st in success rate on defense in the loss on Sunday night.

Title: ABC's High Potential Replacement That's A Perfect Weekend Binge Surges On Streaming At The Best Time
Article_Text:
ABC's High Potential replacement is a crime series that has just surged on multiple streaming services at the perfect time, and it makes for the best weekend binge. High Potential is a major hit on network TV, bringing in millions of viewers each week. It is one of the many shows that form a robust lineup of crime series across different networks. Among those are projects like Nathan Fillion's The Rookie, also an ABC series, which, like High Potential, not only focuses on crime, but does so while balancing humor and personal stakes to make it a multi-layered show.
High Potential became popular due to how its main character, Kaitlin Olson's Morgan Gillory, is not your usual police consultant. With an IQ that makes her an exceptionally gifted individual, Morgan goes from cleaning the floors of the LAPD to solving cases as a consultant. The show veers into a similar tone and territory as previous hit network TV crime series, such as The Mentalist, Castle, and Monk. Now, the show that replaced High Potential on ABC's Tuesdays at 10 PM slot, R.J. Decker, has become a massive hit across three different streaming services, and it happens at the perfect time.
R.J. Decker Is Dominating Multiple Streaming Platforms
At the time of writing, R.J. Decker is trending on Disney+ and Hulu in the United States, as well as finding streaming success on Crave in Canada. R.J. Decker currently stands as the 2nd most-watched TV show on Disney+ in the United States, with the crime series only losing to the fellow genre show The Drop: A Snowfall Saga. R.J. Decker is also the 6th most-watched TV show on Hulu nationwide, where it has left behind popular series like the Glen Powell sports comedy Chad Powers, Gordon Ramsay's Kitchen Nightmares, the hit sitcom It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia, and more.
Hulu's most-watched TV show right now is the reality series Dancing with the Stars. Finally, ABC's R.J. Decker has also proved itself a major hit in Canada, where it currently ranks as the 7th most-watched movie or TV show on Crave's Top 10 Overall chart. It left behind Mark Ruffalo's gritty HBO crime thriller series Task on the streamer. R.J. Decker's streaming dominance comes at the perfect time, as season 2 of the ABC series recently premiered on Tuesday, September 15. R.J. Decker is also a perfect weekend binge, as the show has put out only 10 episodes so far between season 1 and the season 2 premiere.
The Show Is Perfect For High Potential Fans
ABC's High Potential replacement follows former newspaper photographer and prison inmate R.J., who becomes a private investigator after being freed, only he tackles extremely bizarre cases in none other than South Florida, giving it that same sharp edge of High Potential, with a protagonist that is not your usual hard-boiled, straight-faced detective. An R.J. Decker binge on any of the three streaming services it is trending on will have viewers ready for the rest of season 2, and High Potential fans are already used to the time slot the crime series airs, as it was High Potential's first, thus making R.J. Decker its perfect replacement.

Title: Atlanta measles outbreak puts under-vaccinated kids at risk. Here's how to manage it
Article_Text:
Credit:      Sofi Gratas/GPB News
Section Branding
Header Content
Atlanta measles outbreak puts under-vaccinated kids at risk. Here's how to manage it
Primary Content
LISTEN: Measles is extremely contagious and the virus can linger in the air for up to 2 hours. So how do you protect yourself and your kids? GPB's Sofi Gratas explains.
An outbreak of measles linked to a daycare in the metro Atlanta area has infected 10 children, according to the Georgia Department of Public Health.
Meanwhile, health department epidemiologists are working to find who else has been exposed. State officials are withholding the name of the daycare as contact tracing is underway.
Measles is extremely contagious and the virus can linger in the air for up to a couple hours. Every one person with measles can infect an average of 15 people and the risk goes up if people are unvaccinated.
Sher Gardner is an Atlanta-area pediatrician. She says families with under-vaccinated kids may be able to request a measles vaccine from their doctor for children as young as 6 months old.
The vaccine is the same given to kids as part of the typical two-dose set, first at around 12 months old and then between 4 and 6 years old.
"It would not harm the child and it would be protective, especially if a family had reason to believe that their child has increased risk for exposure," Gardner said.
Otherwise, the best practice for worried parents is to stay in, Gardner said — but that doesn't mean a true quarantine.
"When I say stay in, I mean just don't go to places like the fun jumping, bouncing things that all the kids go to," she said. "Those sorts of places where there are lots and lots of children, it may be in their best interest to just wait."
Families should take caution traveling to other states too, especially if there’s been measles reported there.
Measles symptoms can take up to two weeks after exposure to show up. The Department of Public Health is advising that parents with a child who does show symptoms of measles should call ahead to notify healthcare professionals before seeking care outside the home. That’s because doctor’s offices, hospitals and public health departments need to follow specific quarantine procedures.
Georgia’s latest estimated kindergarten vaccination rate — the percent of kids up to 6 years old who are up to date on childhood immunizations including against measles — is 86.8%. That’s still much lower than pre-pandemic levels but a slight increase from the 2021-2022 school year.
- RELATED: With the CDC silent on vaccine guidance, physician-led groups make their own for the upcoming season
Macy McNair is a family physician at the Morehouse School of Medicine. She encourages adult community members to do their part in helping protect vulnerable children by ensuring they themselves are vaccinated.
"We could decrease this outbreak by herd immunity, which is the community doing our part in getting the vaccine," McNair said.
This week, two more measles-associated deaths were reported out of Pennsylvania, which has seen nearly 800 cases so far in 2026. A total of four people, two of them children, have died during the state’s measles outbreak. All were unvaccinated.

Title: Ed Sheeran makes huge change to show tonight after dropping Macklemore from tour
Article_Text:
Ed Sheeran makes huge change to show tonight after dropping Macklemore from tour
Sheeran will perform tonight in Philadelphia for the first time since Macklemore was removed from his Loop tour after his 'Free Palestine' speech
Ed Sheeran has made a significant change to his upcoming concert tonight following the high-profile removal of support act Macklemore from the tour. The 35-year-old singer's tour has dominated headlines in recent days after Macklemore, who had been opening for Sheeran, announced he'd been dropped from the remaining dates.
His removal came after an on-stage speech in which he declared 'Free Palestine'. In a statement, the US rapper claimed that Sheeran had been placed in a difficult position after Gillette Stadium owner Robert Kraft issued an 'ultimatum' regarding his appearance there.
A change has now been made to the British star's upcoming show tonight on Saturday, September 19, at Philadelphia's Lincoln Financial Field. The show marks his first live performance since the controversy erupted, with pro-Palestinian groups reportedly planning demonstrations outside the venue.
Philadelphia Police Department spokesperson Jasmine Reilly confirmed: "Our officers are talking to his team to make sure all appropriate measures are taken' for protection and ensure Sheeran's safety."
The gig had originally been scheduled to kick off at 5.30pm, with Sheeran due on stage at around 8pm. However, Ticketmaster now lists the concert as starting at 8pm, suggesting he may be performing without a support act.
According to TMZ, the award-winning singer is also set to take to the Philadelphia stage without several members of his backing band, who have also pulled out.
Remaining tour dates are still listed as starting at 5.30pm on the ticketing website, though Sheeran is now the sole act on the bill.
The fallout from Macklemore's removal plunged the tour into disarray, with all of Sheeran's support acts subsequently announcing their withdrawal.
Irish singer Aaron Rowe was the first to pull out, quickly followed by Finneas, Beoga, and Danish pop outfit Lukas Graham.
Adding to the turmoil, reports emerged that ticket sales for his Loop Tour have taken a significant hit amid the ongoing controversy, with resale ticket prices steadily declining over recent days.
Macklemore has since vowed to donate his $1m tour earnings to six organisations that are 'working directly to support' people in Palestine.
Ed, meanwhile, released his own statement, claiming it had not been his decision to remove Macklemore from the tour as he insisted it was the promoters who made the call rather than himself.
The Shape of You singer is believed to have lost over 150,000 followers on Instagram in the wake of the fallout.

Title: Lingering feuds threaten Democrats' bid to reclaim US Congress | WSAU News/Talk 550 AM · 99.9 FM
Article_Text:
By Nolan D. McCaskill
WASHINGTON, Sept 19 (Reuters) – Democrats are seeking to reclaim Congress, but lingering divisions from a bruising run-up to the November election threaten to imperil the party’s attempt to claw back power from President Donald Trump’s Republicans.
With control of both chambers at stake, Democrats have sought to move past the bad blood of the primaries, but in several competitive states, influential party figures have withheld endorsements or so far declined to campaign with nominees for the November 3 US midterm elections.
In Maine, the governor has yet to endorse the Democratic US Senate candidate. In Texas, a congresswoman has declined to campaign alongside the state representative who defeated her in the Democratic Senate primary. In Michigan, establishment centrists are steering clear of the party’s progressive Senate pick. In New York, victorious democratic socialists are criticizing congressional Democrats for joining Republicans in condemning socialism. In Florida, the party has yet to rally behind its Senate nominee.
“Whether you are a progressive or an establishment Democrat or a conservative Democrat, we all have a vested interest in getting every single person over the finish line in November,” said US Representative Summer Lee, a progressive Pennsylvania Democrat up for reelection.
If Democrats fail to unify and win at least one chamber, she warned, “all of our work after that is going to be harder.”
Democrats’ best path to a Senate majority requires defeating Susan Collins in Maine. Collins is widely considered the most vulnerable Republican senator in the country. But former Maine Senate President Troy Jackson, the Democratic nominee, is running without the endorsement of Governor Janet Mills, a onetime Senate candidate who hoped to unseat Collins herself. Mills’ office did not respond to a request for comment.
“I would say they’re mostly unified,” Jim Melcher, a political science professor at the University of Maine at Farmington, said of Maine Democrats. “The one piece of it that stands out is that Janet Mills has not endorsed Troy Jackson.”
Contacted by Reuters, the Maine Democratic Party did not directly address Mills’ role but cited turnout for its nominating process and energy on the ground as evidence of unity. “Maine Democrats are united and focused on winning in November,” said Devon Murphy-Anderson, the state party’s executive director. “Troy has spent his career fighting for working Mainers and there is real energy behind his campaign to defeat Susan Collins.”
FORMER RIVALS IN TEXAS
In Texas, US Representative Jasmine Crockett has pledged her support to state Representative James Talarico, who defeated her in the Senate primary and is taking on Republican Ken Paxton. But Crockett has repeatedly rejected Talarico’s overtures for the two to campaign together, even declining to introduce him at Texas Democrats’ state convention in June.
Crockett drew criticism from social media users last week for appearing on stage in Texas with R&B singer Chris Brown, but not with Talarico, who could become the first Democrat in decades to win a statewide race in Texas. In 2009, Brown pleaded guilty to assaulting then-girlfriend Rihanna and has said domestic violence classes helped him learn from his mistakes.
Crockett has instead said she will focus on lower-profile races, arguing that will also benefit Talarico’s Senate campaign.
“As the Democratic nominee, I trust that he has a plan,” Crockett told CBS News this month. “I know that their plan wasn’t necessarily to include his opponent.”
‘FULL SUPPORT’ TO EL-SAYED
In Michigan, lingering divisions have centered on Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed, a progressive who narrowly leads Republican Mike Rogers in polling in one of the party’s must-win states. Some Democrats have expressed discomfort with El-Sayed’s association with controversial streamer Hasan Piker and with his rhetoric on Israel and Jews, and multiple prominent party figures have yet to endorse him.
After their closely contested Senate primary, US Representative Haley Stevens of Michigan offered her “full support” to El-Sayed, and the two hugged at a unity breakfast the following day. An El-Sayed campaign adviser told Reuters the two camps are in regular communication and that the campaign sees Stevens “as a critical member of the coalition that will beat Mike Rogers.”
But it’s unclear whether Stevens will campaign with El-Sayed, and others in the party have been openly critical.
US Representative Hillary Scholten and state Senator Jeremy Moss, the Democratic nominee for a congressional seat, have not endorsed El-Sayed. Neither of their campaigns immediately responded to a request for comment.
Joseph Geevarghese, executive director of Our Revolution – a group that works to elect progressive candidates – said there’s a double-standard when progressives win against establishment candidates.
“The establishment expects progressives to fall in line when they prevail at the ballot box, but when progressives win, there are some signs of unity, but the entire establishment doesn’t really fall in lockstep behind our candidates,” he said. “I think that hurts our ability to do job No. 1, which is to beat the Republicans in November.”
Others see the tensions differently.
“When you run a campaign that completely shits on the establishment and then you win that campaign … then you turn around and say, ‘I need this machine in order to win,’ it is a little bit disingenuous,” Democratic consultant Rodell Mollineau said.
TARGETING DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS ‘LIKE ME’
The divisions surfaced on Capitol Hill earlier this month when eight moderate Democrats joined Republicans in approving a resolution condemning socialism, drawing criticism from New York democratic socialists Darializa Avila Chevalier and Claire Valdez, who are poised to win US House seats in November after defeating establishment-backed rivals in their primaries.
“This resolution was aimed squarely at democratic socialists like me,” Chevalier said in a statement. “We don’t need a tent that shrinks from its own history. We need a unified party that takes on corporate power, gets money out of politics and delivers for working people.”
DISUNITY IN FLORIDA
In Florida, Democratic Senate nominee Angie Nixon, a democratic socialist, defeated the better-funded retired Lieutenant Colonel Alex Vindman by a double-digit margin in August.
Vindman said he would stand beside her “in the fight against” Republican Senator Ashley Moody and has donated $825,000 to help Democratic candidates, including $400,000 to the state party to support Nixon and other Florida Democrats.
But it’s less clear whether the party is as supportive of Nixon as Vindman has been.
Derrick Scott, chair of Florida’s Escambia County Democratic Party, said the party’s “vote blue no matter who” message, shorthand for supporting Democratic candidates, appears to come with an exception now that Nixon is the nominee.
“We still have yet to see Nikki Fried, the chair of the Florida Democratic Party, come out and unequivocally and full-throatedly support Angie Nixon,” he said.
A Democratic Party spokesperson said it’s inaccurate to say the party hasn’t rallied behind Nixon, noting Fried recently joined Nixon and another statewide candidate for a joint press conference. The spokesperson said the party is working closely with Nixon and is frequently in touch with her team.
Chanae Jackson, the Nixon campaign’s former organizing director, said voters are frustrated with party leaders who underestimated Nixon and Democratic organizations too often seek Black voter turnout without building durable support for Black-led campaigns.
“They want our labor, but they don’t want our leadership,” she said. “They want us to work like a dog while they take credit for it.”
(Reporting by Nolan D. McCaskill; Additional reporting by Bianca Flowers; Editing by Michael Learmonth, Andy Sullivan and Howard Goller)

Title: New laws trigger a fresh legal fight over Nazi-looted art in Los Angeles and Auschwitz museums
Article_Text:
LOS ANGELES (AP) — Jewish heirs of Holocaust victims and their representatives have filed two lawsuits in California staking their claims to Nazi-looted paintings that still hang on the walls of prominent museums in Los Angeles and Auschwitz.
This pair of lawsuits are the first to be filed after the recent passage of laws by California and Congress, which strengthen U.S.-based claims to artwork that were forcibly taken from Jewish families during World War II.
One lawsuit was filed in Los Angeles Superior Court on Monday by the Jewish Federation of Greater Los Angeles and its board chair Daniel Gryczman against Norton Simon Museum in Pasadena for the return of “Adam and Eve.” These are two life-size oil-on-panel masterpieces created by Lucas Carnach the Elder in 1530.
The other lawsuit was filed in federal court in Los Angeles the same day by the daughters of the late Dinah Gottliebova Babbitt, a Holocaust survivor and California-based animator who was held in Auschwitz. It demanded the return of watercolors of fellow prisoners that the artist was forced to paint for Josef Mengele, a Nazi physician who had earned the nickname the “Angel of Death.”
Spokespersons for both museums say the museums legally hold titles to the works, and intend to continue displaying them to the public. The lawsuits don’t specify the monetary value of the paintings.
Artworks pit Jewish families against museums
The issue of Nazi-looted art is an emotional, legally and ethically charged topic that pits Jewish families that have suffered inter-generational trauma against museums that say they are trying to preserve a painful, yet important, chapter of history. Between 1933 and 1945, the Nazi regime orchestrated the largest art theft in world history, seizing over 600,000 works of art across Europe from Jewish families, collectors and museums. Decades later, many of these masterpieces reside in prominent museums around the world, making the push for their recovery more complex than a simple property dispute.
Rabbi Noah Farkas is president and CEO of the Jewish Federation of Los Angeles, the organization to which Marei von Saher, sole heir of Dutch Jewish art dealer Jacques Goudstikker, has signed over her rights. The paintings were seized from Goudstikker's collection by Hermann Goring, Adolf Hitler’s second-in-command and changed a number of hands before being sold in the 1960s to the Pasadena Museum of Modern Art, which was renamed Norton Simon Museum in honor of its benefactor.
Farkas said the federation plans to use most of the net proceeds from the recovered art to provide much-needed help to the about 2,500 Holocaust survivors living in the Los Angeles area.
“These are incredibly beautiful European masterpieces stolen from a Jewish family to enrich the Nazi party and fund the war and death machine against the people,” he said. “It's our honor to take on this role on behalf of the community and use most of the proceeds to help these elderly survivors live out the last years of their lives in dignity, comfort and peace – something their family members were denied during the Holocaust.”
Marei von Saher, in a statement, said she is grateful to the Jewish organization for taking up her family’s cause.
“This effort represents a meaningful step toward justice for Holocaust survivors and victims of Nazi era atrocities,” she said.
New legislation gives lawsuits second wind
California Assemblyman Jesse Gabriel, D-Woodland Hills, wrote Assembly Bill 2867, signed by Gov. Gavin Newsom in September 2024, which requires that the state law must apply in lawsuits brought by California residents or their heirs to recover art seized during the Holocaust or during other acts of persecution. Gabriel, who co-chairs the California Legislative Jewish Caucus, introduced the legislation in response to a federal court ruling, which allowed the state-owned Thyssen-Bornemisza National Museum in Madrid to keep a multimillion-dollar Camille Pissarro impressionist masterpiece.
That painting had been taken by the Nazis from the Cassirer family in 1939. This case, which prompted this new law, is expected to be heard in federal court in California next month.
Gabriel said it’s time for museums to “do some deep introspection on whether they want to be on the right side of history.”
Museums want to preserve paintings for posterity
Norton Simon Museum released a statement pointing out that a federal court in 2018 unanimously determined that the museum had proper title to the Cranach paintings. In May 2019, the U.S. Supreme Court declined to get involved in the case, leaving in place lower court rulings.
They said the Cranach paintings, which originally belonged to the Stroganoff family, were put up for sale in 1931 by the Soviet Union in an illicit auction in Berlin where they were purchased by Goudstikker. After a complicated journey, the paintings were sold to the museum by a Stroganoff family descendant. The museum later restored and preserved the pieces.
“For nearly 50 years, they have been on view at the Norton Simon Museum and will continue to be accessible to the public for years to come,” the statement said.
Pawel Sawicki, a spokesperson for the Auschwitz Memorial, said the watercolors of Roma victims that Gottliebova Babbitt was forced to paint by Mengele to document his horrendous experiments and racial research, “must remain in the Memorial” to document the man's crimes. He said these paintings must not be mischaracterized as “Nazi-looted art” because Gottliebova Babbitt painted them against her will as a prisoner and therefore didn’t have ownership of the watercolors.
While he understands the family’s sentiments, Sawicki said the portraits of Roma and Sinti victims are among the few remaining documents of Mengele’s criminal experiments and should be treated as unique documents related to the history of the Auschwitz concentration camp.
“While fully respecting the rights of people who created some of the documents here, we are of the opinion that any loss in the collections of the Memorial will constitute irreparable harm,” he said. “ … The loss of even the smallest part of the documentation is an irreparable loss and blemish on the memory of the victims of Auschwitz.”
Advocates hope cases will now be heard on their merit
Joel Greenberg, founder of Art Ashes, a Philadelphia-area nonprofit that helps Jewish families track down and recover Nazi-looted art, said in addition to the California law, President Donald Trump signed into law and updated the Holocaust Expropriated Art Recovery Act of 2025. This new law permanently eliminated the expiration date to allow Holocaust survivors and their heirs to indefinitely pursue the recovery of these works of art.
Greenberg said the new federal law gave families the right to reclaim their art for up to six years from the time they find out in whose possession they are.
“These new laws mean that technical defenses will no longer stick in court,” he said. “Every case will be heard on its merits.”
He said the new legislation also ensures that these Jewish families have their day in court and a fair process to determine ownership of the stolen art.
“It will make sure the stories of what happened to European Jewry is not lost and forgotten,” he said. “The art can still be returned to the rightful owner.”

Title: Five college prospects who could interest the Eagles in the 2027 NFL Draft
Article_Text:
September 19, 2026
During the college football season each year, as long as you're watching the games, we point out five players each week to keep an eye on who make logical sense for the Philadelphia Eagles in the following year's NFL Draft.
Miller is a big-bodied receiver at 6'2, 215 who averaged at least 18.0 yards per catch in each of his first three college seasons at Colorado before transferring to ASU. In 2025 at Colorado, he had 45 catches for 808 yards and 8 TDs.
Miller doesn't have elite speed, but he can track the ball down the field, he wins contested catches, and he has some run after catch ability.
Also, love this block way down the field on a TD in ASU's Week 1 win over Morgan State:
The Eagles could use a bigger guy to add to their small group of receivers.
Rhodes has great length at 6'6 with long arms. In 2025, Rhodes had 42 tackles (15.5 for loss), 8 sacks, and 1 FF. He only has 9 sacks for his college career. NFL teams will want to see numbers again this season to put any production concerns to bed, but the traits are there.
Video via @NoFlagsFilm:
His body movements and length give me some Josh Sweat vibes.
🚨Jimmy fave alert.
Knapp played LT his first two seasons at Notre Dame, replacing Joe Alt. In 2026, he's playing LG, and in his first game against Wisconsin, he had a season's worth of pancakes.
Knapp is versatile and tough. The Eagles are going to have interest.
If Tyler Steen leaves in free agency and Landon Dickerson's body simply can't function any longer then the Eagles may need to replace both guards next offseason. They have to like what they saw from Drew Kendall and Willie Lampkin in training camp, but guard remains a potential need position.
Echoles' first year as a starter was in 2025, and he had a big season, making 68 tackles (11.5 for loss), 5 sacks, and 5 batted passes. He's quick and powerful, with legitimate pass rush chops. Impressive video below, via @NoFlagsFilm. Watch him win with an assortment of moves, but also play the run well, and chase down plays on the perimeter.
The Eagles have Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis under contract long-term, but they are likely to lose Moro Ojomo in free agency next offseason. The Eagles highly value the interior of their D-line, and Echoles would make sense as a guy who could fill right in for Ojomo.
Green is one of the most impressive athletes in college football. He's a tight end for the football team, and was briefly a forward for the basketball team.
As a football player, he is gifted with 6'7 height and impressive body control. He is a 50-50 ball beast with enormous upside.
Green is more of a big receiver than a complete tight end at the moment, so, you know, it would be kind of insane for the Eagles to use a high pick on him after they selected Eli Stowers in the second round of the 2026 draft. But I don't care. He's a cool player and I wanted to profile him.

Title: MLB roundup: Braves top Astros, wrap up postseason berth
Article_Text:
Field Level Media
                
19 Sep 2026, 13:25 GMT+10
            
(Photo credit: Troy Taormina)
Michael Harris II, Ronald Acuna Jr. and Matt Olson slugged two-run home runs and deadline acquisition Tyler Mahle continued his exceptional pitching for the visiting Atlanta Braves, who secured a postseason berth with a 6-2 victory over the Houston Astros on Friday.
Atlanta qualified for the postseason for the eighth time in nine seasons. The Braves lowered their magic number to clinch the National League East to three over the Philadelphia Phillies.
Harris provided Mahle a 2-0 lead when he followed a one-out single by Matt Olson with an opposite-field blast to left off Astros starter Peter Lambert (8-10) in the fourth inning. Harris (3-for-5) drove a first-pitch slurve from Lambert 367 feet for his 26th homer of the year.
Mahle (7-10) improved to 4-1 with a 1.28 ERA over eight starts since his acquisition from the Giants. He allowed one run on three hits and one walk with six strikeouts over six innings.
Guardians 5, Athletics 3
Jose Ramirez hit a solo homer in the sixth inning for his 1,000th career RBI after rookie Travis Bazzana went deep in the fifth, fueling host Cleveland to a victory over the Athletics.
The Guardians have won three in a row to move a game ahead of the second-place Chicago White Sox in the American League Central. Joey Cantillo (10-9) threw six scoreless innings in relief, and Cade Smith handled the ninth for his 38th save.
Zack Gelof belted a three-run homer in the first inning for the Athletics, whose losing skid reached four games. Reliever Scott Blewett (2-1) permitted one run on one hit in 1 2/3 innings.
Padres 8, Marlins 2
Ty France clouted a three-run homer to cap a six-run fifth inning as San Diego stopped visiting Miami to forge a three-way tie atop the National League wild-card standings.
Winning for the 11th time in 12 games, the Padres pulled even with the Chicago Cubs and Philadelphia Phillies, who both lost. San Diego's magic number for clinching a playoff spot dropped to four.
San Diego starter Nick Pivetta (3-2) worked five innings, yielding four hits and a run. Marlins reliever Cade Gibson (5-2) was charged with the first two runs in the game-changing fifth. The Padres' Jackson Merrill and the Marlins' Agustin Ramirez homered.
Mets 6, Phillies 3
Zac Thornton tossed six solid innings, Juan Soto homered among his three hits and host New York beat Philadelphia.
Soto went 3-for-5 for the Mets, while Francisco Lindor and Carson Benge each collected two hits. Thornton (5-5) gave up two runs on five hits.
Edmundo Sosa finished 3-for-3 with a homer and Derek Hill also went deep for the Phillies, who fell to 7-9 this month. Newly acquired Jose Urquidy threw 4 2/3 shutout innings after opener Tim Mayza (3-4) surrendered three runs while getting just one out.
Reds 6, Cubs 4
Cincinnati scored three times in the sixth inning in a back-and-forth win over visiting Chicago.
Elly De La Cruz had two hits, two walks and two runs for the Reds. Cincinnati starter Chase Burns and reliever Julian Aguiar (1-0) each allowed two runs on four hits in three innings.
Cubs starter Clay Holmes (6-8) surrendered six runs on three hits in 5 1/3 innings. Ian Happ homered for Chicago, and Michael Conforto amassed three hits.
Twins 3, Angels 0
Connor Prielipp allowed two hits over a career-high seven innings and fellow rookie Walker Jenkins went 3-for-4 with a home run as Minnesota topped Los Angeles in Anaheim, Calif.
Travis Adams pitched a 1-2-3 ninth inning to pick up his third save. Jenkins, who began his career going 4-for-45, homered for the second straight game on his sixth consecutive hit in the series.
Jose Siri had two hits for the Angels. Grayson Rodriguez (4-8) gave up three runs on eight hits in 6 2/3 innings.
Brewers 6, Orioles 5 (10 innings)
Sal Frelick singled home a 10th-inning run and visiting Milwaukee pulled out a victory against Baltimore.
Trevor Megill (3-3) was the winning pitcher despite a blown save. Chad Patrick retired the Orioles in order in the bottom of the 10th for his sixth save.
Milwaukee's Jackson Chourio and Baltimore's Pete Alonso hit three-run homers early in the game. Gunnar Henderson and Coby Mayo both collected three hits for the Orioles.
Dodgers 8, Giants 2
Mookie Betts homered twice, including his 53rd career leadoff homer, and Josue De Paula hit a tiebreaking double to help Los Angeles produce a victory over visiting San Francisco.
The Dodgers socked five home runs while winning for the 12th time in the last 15 games. Max Muncy and Kyle Tucker hit back-to-back homers in the eighth, and Betts and Will Smith repeated the feat later in the frame. Tyler Glasnow (5-1) gave up two runs and three hits while striking out a season-high 10 in six innings.
Jung Hoo Lee homered and Jonah Cox had an RBI single as the Giants fell for the fifth time in seven games.
Yankees 9, Diamondbacks 2
George Lombard Jr. had two hits and three RBIs, and his two-run single capped a five-run first-inning outburst as New York cruised past Arizona in Phoenix.
Ben Rice and Lombard homered and Rice added a triple as the Yankees won for the fourth time in five games. Gerrit Cole (9-9) gave up two runs on four hits in six innings.
Corbin Carroll homered and doubled for the Diamondbacks, who have lost five of six to see their NL wild-card chances fade. Eduardo Rodriguez (15-7) yielded seven runs in 5 1/3 innings.
Red Sox 4, Rays 2
Roman Anthony homered and had three RBIs, Jahmai Jones went deep and Boston cooled off first-place Tampa Bay in St. Petersburg, Fla.
Anthony went 2-for-5 while Caleb Durbin was 2-for-3 for the Red Sox. Boston starter Ranger Suarez (8-4) fought control issues but allowed one run on three hits in 5 2/3 innings.
Junior Caminero doubled, walked twice and drove in a run for the Rays, who had only five hits as their six-game winning streak ended. Ian Seymour (9-7) allowed four runs on seven hits in five innings.
Rangers 7, Blue Jays 1
Corey Seager capped a four-run second inning with an RBI double as Texas topped Toronto in Arlington, Texas.
The Rangers drew 10 walks and moved into a first-place tie with Houston in the American League West. Jake Burger had two RBIs for Texas, which won for the fifth time in six games. Texas took a 4-0 lead in the second inning against Dylan Cease (11-6), who allowed four runs (one earned) on three hits over 2 2/3 innings.
The Blue Jays fell two games back of the White Sox for the final AL wild-card spot. Myles Straw had two hits with an RBI for Toronto, which committed three errors and lost for the third time in four games.
Tigers 11, White Sox 8
Dillon Dingler delivered the go-ahead single and Riley Greene followed with a two-run homer in a five-run eighth inning as visiting Detroit stormed back from six runs down to beat Chicago.
Hao-Yu Lee went 4-for-5 with a homer, three RBIs and two runs for the Tigers. Kevin McGonigle finished 2-for-5 with four RBIs. Drew Sommers (2-4) threw two shutout innings, fanning five, and Kenley Jansen blanked the White Sox in the ninth for his 21st save.
Colson Montgomery and Miguel Vargas each had two hits and three RBIs for the White Sox, who have lost three out of four. Sean Newcomb (2-5) got only two outs in relief while allowing three runs.
Pirates 8, Royals 5
Konnor Griffin had four hits and two RBIs and Spencer Horwitz delivered a tiebreaking two-run single in the seventh as Pittsburgh rallied to beat visiting Kansas City.
Pittsburgh trailed 4-0 after the top of the third inning and 5-2 entering the bottom of the fourth. The Pirates won their second straight after losing four of their previous five.
Vinnie Pasquantino and Michael Massey each homered as the Royals scored five runs against Pittsburgh ace Paul Skenes, who scattered six hits in his six innings. Royals starter Randy Dobnak allowed four runs on seven hits over 3 2/3 innings.
Nationals 9, Cardinals 1
Cade Cavalli pitched five scoreless innings and recorded the 200th strikeout of his first full major league season, leading Washington to a victory at St. Louis.
Cavalli (13-5), who agreed with the Nationals earlier in the day on a four-year, $47 million contract extension, allowed four hits and struck out six. Dylan Crews hit a two-run homer and Yohandy Morales added a two-run double for Washington.
Cardinals starter Kyle Leahy (10-5) allowed seven runs, six earned, on five hits over three innings. Leo Bernal went 3-for-4.
Mariners 5, Rockies 4
Lazaro Montes homered leading off the top of the ninth, J.P. Crawford went deep to open the game, and Seattle beat Colorado in Denver.
Randy Arozarena finished with three hits as the Mariners logged their second win in a row. Carlos Vargas (2-0) recorded one out in relief, and Andres Munoz earned his 28th save with a scoreless ninth inning.
Cole Carrigg, Connor Norby and Jake McCarthy had three hits apiece and Ezequiel Tovar contributed two hits for the Rockies, who have lost three in a row and 11 of 12. Jordan Romano (0-4) served up Montes' homer.

Title: Pueblo in line for a 40-acre greenhouse complex producing lettuce
Article_Text:
From the early 1920s to the mid-1950s, South-Central Colorado was such a crucial source of produce that Buena Vista enjoyed a two-decade run as the “Head Lettuce Capital of the World.”
That “green gold rush” ended when innovations in refrigeration and shipping technology gave California an unbeatable edge.
But southern Colorado could once again see a lettuce comeback, just a little further to the east, with technological advances and high fuel costs tipping the advantage back in the state’s favor.
An unnamed hydroponic grower, applying as Project Deep Root, received state approval on Thursday morning for $2.75 million in Job Growth Incentive Tax Credits tied to 413 new jobs in Pueblo County.
The company plans to spend $320 million on a 40-acre greenhouse complex that will grow lettuce without soil and pesticides.
Michelle Hadwiger, director of global business development at the Colorado Office of Economic Development and International Trade, pitched the project to the Colorado Economic Development Commission as “Colorado’s largest controlled environment agricultural project.”
Project Deep Root is considering alternative locations in Idaho, Tennessee and Pennsylvania. Those sites suggest the applicant is likely Little Leaf Farms, which is based in Devens, Mass.
Besides a 60-acre complex in Devens, the company has a 30-acre greenhouse in McAdoo, Pa., and an 80-acre complex under construction in Manchester, Tenn.
Little Leaf Farms raised $300 million in 2022 from investors to build a national footprint and disrupt California growers who ship their products thousands of miles.
With average diesel prices now above $6.28 a gallon in the U.S., transportation costs have become critical for all agricultural producers.
A spokesman for Project Deep Root told the commission that the Pueblo facility would target markets within a two-day drive, which aligns with Little Leaf Farms’ goal of reaching store shelves within 24 hours after harvest.
Safety and sustainability are also part of the company’s pitch.
Repeated outbreaks, most recently from the parasite Cyclospora, have put open-field farms under scrutiny. Little Leaf Farms uses rainwater collected on its roofs and sanitized with UV treatments to eliminate pathogens.
It also claims it can produce lettuce using 90% less water than conventional open farm methods, a selling point in a drought-stricken state like Colorado.
Colorado’s colder climate, however, leaves greenhouses at a disadvantage. Little Leaf Farms uses a newer insulated glass that allows for efficient year-round operations in colder climates.
Apart from cloudy days, its greenhouses rely on natural light, which should help shield it from higher electricity prices that have squeezed fully indoor vertical farms like 80 Acres Farm, which shut down its Aurora operations last month.
Ladybugs provide the minimal pest control needed, avoiding harmful chemicals. From planted seed to finished head, no human hand touches the production during its automated run, according to the company’s website.
Project Deep Root said it would pay its workers an average annual wage of $56,910, which matches the average wage in Pueblo County. That was on the low end of the five companies approved for incentives Thursday, resulting in a relatively smaller award.
Average wages offered by photonics and quantum computing firms looking at Boulder County were two to three times higher. But the sheer number of jobs should have a meaningful impact on Pueblo’s manufacturing economy.
The San Luis Valley and northern New Mexico, with their sandy soils, cool night temperatures, and rail access, became a core growing area for Crisphead lettuce a century ago.
The harvested lettuce heads were packed in heavy wooden crates with ice, which crews hauled from mountain lakes during the winter.
Those crates, frozen together into large icy masses after shipping on railcars, would result in Crisphead becoming rebranded as Iceberg.
The Colorado fields primarily filled the summer gap, when temperatures were too hot in Arizona and California.
Improvements in commercial vacuum cooling allowed California growers to chill their lettuce in under 30 minutes without the use of ice, eliminating a key advantage Colorado had.
As the green gold faded away, farmers in the San Luis Valley reverted to growing potatoes again.

Title: Fights and weapons confiscations are down in Philly schools
Article_Text:
September 19, 2026
With a new school year underway, School District of Philadelphia Chief of Safety Craig Johnson is determined to maintain the downward trends he's been seeing in student violence.
The number of weapons confiscated from students dropped about 67%, from 516 in the 2021-2022 school year to 171 in the 2024-2025 school year, according to district-provided data. Knives are the most commonly found weapons, and firearms typically account for about 4% of confiscated weapons.
The total number of student assaults and fights dipped 22% districtwide from 2021 to 2025, according to a Chalkbeat analysis of serious incident reports.
Still, parents have expressed worries about violence throughout the year, arguing that the district's plan to shutter 17 campuses in fall 2027 could escalate existing tensions between students from different schools.
Johnson said his team has been working to build a culture of safety in Philadelphia schools, from training a small faction of the district's school safety officers in conflict mediation to offering post-fight "stabilization groups" and ongoing care sessions through a partnership with the city's behavioral health department.
John Bartram High School in West Philadelphia uses a model called the Youth Violence Reduction Initiative, which provides mentorship and case management to students at risk of violence, and saw significant drops in both fighting and gun violence perpetrated by students.
The district also works with local organizations such as the Philadelphia Anti-Gang, Anti-Violence Network, or PAAN, for help breaking up campus fights and preventing street violence near schools.
Chalkbeat Philadelphia spoke with Johnson about what's worked and what's next.
This interview has been edited for length and clarity.
Why do you think these incident numbers have been trending down?
Our training changed, and so we really focus on building relationships with students and meeting them where they are … allowing us to be more proactive and intervene prior to violence occurring.
When does the school district partner with outside organizations to train staff or mediate conflict?
Sometimes the concern is when adults are involved. We're equipped to handle children. When you have adults involved as well, we need a little outside assistance. Getting folks in a room and just having a discussion and trying to iron out what the issue is. And getting everybody to come to some common agreements of how they're going to comport themselves and behave themselves.
What are some of the primary channels where you hear about a conflict brewing between students?
We firmly believe every child needs an anchor. At least one anchor, and that's a person that you can go to to talk to about anything, without fear of judgment or reprisal. And I think our department and the district as a whole has done a really good job of making that the culture in our schools. I don't believe there's a student out there in any school that doesn't have at least one adult in that building that they're comfortable talking to. And so the majority of our information comes from students who think something may be wrong. Students don't want to see violence.
What’s happening to keep things calm at dismissal?
We all know that fights can happen at any time. Sometimes we have advance notice of a potential issue at dismissal time. … Or if there had been some kind of an altercation in school during the day that we're aware of, we will usually bolster our presence outside, either through the use of our patrol resources or some support from the Philadelphia Police Department, who we share an absolutely tremendous working relationship with. They provide outstanding support to the school district on a daily basis.
What else is on the horizon?
I'm just looking forward to a great school year. I'm very hopeful that the numbers continue to trend downward as they have for the last couple of years, and we will continue to work with our men and women to be a big part of that.
This story is part of a collaboration between Chalkbeat Philadelphia and The New York Times’s Headway Initiative, supported by the Stavros Niarchos Foundation (SNF) via the Local Media Foundation. Title: Has hope already left the Cowboys? | The Victoria Advocate
Article_Text:
Has hope already left the Cowboys?
Published 5:15 am Saturday, September 19, 2026
|                            Getting your Trinity Audio player ready...                        | 
With questions surrounding its defense after game one, the Dallas Cowboys will be down two defensive starters as they return home to face the Washington Commanders Sunday at 3:25 p.m.
Linebacker DeMarvion Overshown strained his right hamstring in the Cowboys’ 28-20 loss at the New York Giants. He did not participate in Wednesday’s practice and is expected to miss 1-2 weeks. Overshown has missed major time since his rookie season in 2024, and was limited to just six games last season.
The Dallas defensive backs took a hit as well, as safety Malik Hooker had surgery on a fractured forearm this week. The hope is he will be out no longer than two weeks. Hooker and Overshown are expected to bring veteran experience to a Cowboys defense that is brimming with new faces, and therefore, susceptible to mistakes.
The Cowboys gave up scoring drives of 55, 74, and 65 yards to the Giants. Linebackers were still getting into position as the Giants snapped the ball.
Rookie linebacker Jaishawn Barham appeared disheveled on the sidelines during a conversation with first year defensive coordinator Christan Parker. Both Parker and Barham are in roles that are new to them. Schottenheimer says the mistakes are “part of the learning curve.”
“He will learn from this,” said Schottenheimer when asked about Parker, “ just like our young players are going to learn from this.
“We did not perform well as a football team,” added Schottenheimer, “but I’m also not ready to say the expectations for where we’re going to get to as a football team and a defense are not accurate.”
Washington heads to Jerry World on the heels of a 24-22 loss at the Philadelphia Eagles. Although his stats will not win many hi-5’s, quarterback Jayden Daniels threw for an efficient 164 yards and two touchdowns. Instead, Washington will attempt to replicate the Giants success of running the football on the Cowboys. Against the Eagles, Washington controlled the ball for 33:20 minutes to Philadelphia’s 26:40.
It means that Barham, the linebackers, and the rest of the front seven need to prepare for a Washington team that rushed for 132 yards and a touchdown. Cowboy’s defensive tackle Quinnen Williams signed a 3-year $105.9 million deal in the offseason to plug run gaps, but the Giants averaged 4.5 yards per carry with two rushing touchdowns. Dallas mustered just three tackles for loss.
“I can do more,” admitted Williams. “I can be more disruptive in the backfield.”
While it would be unwise to label a Week 2 game in the NFL a “must win,” Sunday’s matchup is pretty important. A loss against Washington means an 0-2 start not just to the season, but in the division.
“We got to look in the mirror as a defense,” said Williams. “We have the guys on this defensive unit to be accountable and to get better.”

Title: FEASTIVAL 2026 brings 25+ Philadelphia restaurants, bars and live performances to FringeArts
Article_Text:
September 19, 2026
FEASTIVAL will turn FringeArts into a mix of tasting room and performance space on Wednesday, Oct. 28, with food and drink offerings from more than 25 Philadelphia restaurants and bars alongside live performances throughout the venue.
Rather than separating dinner and entertainment into different parts of the night, performances will happen among attendees and, in some cases, above the crowd. Brian Sanders’ JUNK is among the artists announced so far, with more performers expected to be added.
The lineup includes South Philly Barbacoa/Casa México, Fork, a.kitchen, Post Haste, Irwin’s, High Street, Grace & Proper, Franklin Fountain, Kiddo, Manong, Habibi, Wilder and more.
Cristina Martinez, Ari Miller and Rue Landau will co-host the event, which begins at 7 p.m. at FringeArts and Fringe Bar, 140 N. Columbus Blvd.
General admission tickets cost $200 for the 7 p.m. main event, which features food and drink offerings from participating restaurants and bars alongside live performances and installations. VIP tickets cost $350 and include entry at 6 p.m., plus exclusive bites and special performances.
The format brings food, drink tastings and live entertainment together in one night, with attendees moving through the venue as different performances take place around them.
Creative cocktail attire is suggested.
FEASTIVAL is celebrating its 15th year and serves as FringeArts’ largest annual fundraiser. Proceeds benefit FringeArts programming and the Fringe Festival.
Date: Wednesday, Oct. 28
Main event: 7-9:30 p.m.
VIP entry: 6 p.m.
Location: FringeArts + Fringe Bar
Address: 140 N. Columbus Blvd., Philadelphia 19106
General admission: $200
VIP admission: $350
Food and drink: More than 25 participating restaurants and bars announced
Entertainment: Live performances and installations, including Brian Sanders’ JUNK
Co-hosts: Cristina Martinez, Ari Miller and Rue Landau
Dress: Creative cocktail
Beneficiary: FringeArts programming and the Fringe Festival
